$comment: The one maintained description of the wand. Edit it with the device or receiver change, run python3 scripts/build.py, then npm test. Tests compare these values with the real sources. The buttons are the speech, HUD and mouse buttons (formerly Top, Middle and Bottom); their ids top, middle and bottom, keys T, M and B, and middleReportDelayMs keep the earlier names for compatibility.
name: Magic Wand
tagline: Mouse, HUD, scrolling and speech to text from three buttons on a wand.
summary: Turning the wand moves my Mac’s pointer or the Agentic Mouse HUD outline. A Puck.js at the tip reads the rotation and sends it over Bluetooth.

vision.headline: The age of AI doesn’t need a keyboard.
vision.detail: The wand is my step toward that. It’s not a mouse replacement: lounge back with the wand and ask Computer Use for most things, ideally by talking through Hello Chat, then reach for your mouse and Agentic Mouse when you need precision. Keep the keyboard for text that has to be typed exactly, which I find is rare.

notes: The installed wand uses a radial HUD with Switch App in the centre. The browser demo retains its earlier grid.
The browser demo shows the main HUD; native app-specific controls and desk detection need the installed integrations.

Ordinary actions act once and keep the HUD open on the same card, so you can select as many times as you want. Only a double click, Close or locking the Mac closes it; every open page’s centre says “Double click to close”. Exceptions: Screenshot parks the HUD for its crosshair; a quick tap from closed on Switch App and the held Switch App chooser switch and close; Review changes and Stage files hide the HUD for review. Unheld wand movement moves the outline; click the HUD button to use the outlined wedge. There is no inactivity timeout. The mouse and speech buttons remain independent.

Adjustable cards are held only: click or release on one to select it (dots), then hold the HUD button and move to adjust it; releasing stops so the wand can reset, and nothing listens while the HUD button is up. Each card’s arrows show its direction: values move up and down; Spaces, Horizontal Scroll, Magnet, tabs, chat and cursor history and Tracks move left and right; Mission Control and similar actions act once per quick held swipe. Tracks keeps its click. Copy/Paste has no click on the wand; Space is its own outer card beyond Enter. Switch App: a tap switches once; in an open HUD a fresh hold on it chooses apps by moving left or right, and release switches.

The wand home ring is grouped, clockwise from 12: the app card, Utility, Play/Pause, YouTube, Horizontal Scroll, Forward, Back, Enter, Copy/Paste, New Codex chat, Close and Keys. These positions stay the same in every app. Keys puts ← ↑ ↓ → across the top; Utility mirrors home, with Zoom beside Brightness. A second outer layer holds quick actions one reach further out on the same wedge: a thin Undo beyond Keys, Space beyond Enter, and, only while VS Code is frontmost, larger Review changes and Stage files beyond the app card. Zoom is a third layer beyond Utility. On the wand, cell 10 reads Close and never holds Command, cell 5 reads Forward without the mice’s volume chord, and Codex Pin/Unpin has no Hold 2 cue. The physical mice are unchanged.
The mouse, HUD and speech buttons are independent. Mouse follow can keep running while review is selected.

In VS Code, go out past the app card and tap Review changes or Stage files to enter and hide the HUD. Move through a rough quarter-circle or diamond corner: clockwise for one next step, anticlockwise for one previous step, with no button held. A full loop gives four steps; straight up/down flicks are disabled. Tap the HUD button once to cancel and exit after at most 300 ms, double-click to switch between Review changes and Stage files, retaining the selection and including the current file without staging, or hold it for about half a second to stage the working selection and keep reviewing. Navigation stays frozen until release. The floating indicator says “Hold to stage selection” and names the mode a double-click will enter. Review changes uses Better Git eyes mode; Stage files uses its whole-file selection.
Review input only runs while VS Code is frontmost. The small review indicator stays above Agent Flow.
The native wand home HUD has Play/Pause after Utility around the ring. It uses the Mac’s standard media key, without changing either physical mouse.

Keep moving the wand slightly while you are not certain about placement so it does not click. Stop when you are ready. The pointer must still be moving; tiny movements filtered out as hand noise do not prevent a click.
Tap while following
Stop following without clicking
Hold
Over a scroll area, drag to scroll. Holding still continues page scrolling; sideways swipes end when the stroke stops. A confirmed draggable target drags instead. Release stops the gesture.
Tap, then hold the second press
Drag with the mouse button down; release to drop
Double tap
Centre the pointer on the main screen and enable mouse follow after the 300 ms triple-tap window; keep HUD and review selection unchanged
Triple tap

notes: Control V3 keeps ordinary short taps and tap-then-hold dragging unchanged. Clear sideways flicks can qualify before the usual 220 ms hold cutoff; other gestures keep that cutoff.

A plain hold scrolls a scroll area or drags a confirmed draggable target. Unknown targets keep scrolling. Tap, then hold the second press to drag explicitly. The pointer stays fixed while scrolling until release.
The HUD button switches to the HUD. The pointer stays within real display edges.
Releasing a completed scroll restores the mouse-follow choice from before scrolling: off stays off and on stays on.
The mouse button never opens, closes or clears the HUD or review selection.

V3 uses straight strokes in either axis, including diagonals. Holding still continues the captured speed; a new stroke can change speed or reverse without releasing. Much faster strokes go beyond the normal maximum, up to 600 lines per second. Circular page-scroll recognition is disabled; V2 remains selectable.

Screenshot opens the native macOS selection and moves the pointer even with mouse follow off. After a triple tap, hold the mouse button and move to select the area, then release to capture. Finishing or cancelling restores the previous mouse-follow choice.

orientationCompensation.scope: Shared correction for mouse, HUD selection, held actions, review and scrolling. Wrist roll and elevated-tip heading correction run before screen-axis gains, with heading correction capped at 2x. No new movement buffer.

sustainedScroll.scope: V3 page scrolling emits precise pixels with fractional travel at the existing20ms cadence and no history-swipe phase. Fine speed and repeated flick increments retain their rate. Pure horizontal V3 output keeps native gesture phases, ends on wrist stop and has no stillness continuation. V2 and chords keep their existing wheel transport.
sustainedScroll.sameDirectionPageFlicks: Each distinct qualified same-direction page flick adds to the held speed, capped at1200 lines/second; deceleration does not lower it.

earlyHorizontalIntent.scope: V3 clear sideways flicks only. The existing stroke classifier must already be active and purely horizontal, with the target resolved to scrolling. Ordinary taps, vertical and diagonal page scrolling, and dragging keep the 220 ms hold cutoff. Accepted short swipes cannot become clicks on release. No pointer delay is added; physical acceptance is pending.

flickScroll.description: Optional: in HIGH mouse mode with the mouse button released, flick up then lower slowly to scroll up. The pointer stays put during the gesture.

sensePointer.scope: Sense profile only. Direct uses the calibrated, orientation-projected gyro rate with the configured gain, 1.4 vertical gain and one-third held gain. It retains about 8 ms of causal smoothing, the original speed-based sensitivity curve, a quiet-stop floor and a bounded step for late readings; it does not replay missed motion. The experimental sub-threshold fine-motion bypass is disabled. Stop-to-click and screenshot settling retain the tuned stop detection. feature-flags.json "sensePointer": "tuned" or Options > Pointer filtering returns to the tuned filter. The Puck always uses the tuned filter.

microCircles.scope: Review navigation counts rough quarter-turns by angle and retains the known circle size through pauses and about-faces to reject small reverse wobbles. A near-complete coherent smaller circle can relearn its size; after a dramatic size reduction the first loop may establish the new size. Held scrolling, pointer gains, filters, sensor rate and motion-delay settings remain unchanged.

reviewAxisGestures.title: Review with nods and shakes
reviewAxisGestures.scope: Optional replacement for quarter-turn review navigation. Every clear vertical turn advances; every horizontal turn goes previous. The first step needs an outward motion and a reversal. Continued back-and-forth movement counts each new turn. Pointer, HUD and speech are unchanged.

tuning.manualPowerChord: All three grip buttons turn off; any single button wakes. Release all before another action.
